facts.raw_span: an 8-month history of radicular pain radiating from her lower back down the left leg
occasional tingling
denied any weakness, autonomic symptoms, history of trauma, or injury
mild hypesthesia in the left L5–S1 dermatome
normal muscle strength, normal abduction and adduction
negative Lasègue, Kernig, Bragard, and Sicard signs
Electromyography showed neuropathic irritation of the left L4, L5, S1, and S2 roots
most severe at L5, with no denervation
a solitary, completely cystic mass in the left L5–S1 foraminal zone
measuring approximately 13.9 cm in length and 1.9 cm in maximal diameter
hypointense on T1-weighted images, hyperintense on T2-weighted images, and demonstrated peripheral rim enhancement
causing severe foraminal stenosis without attachment to pelvic organs
MR neurography confirmed that the mass arose from the sciatic nerve at the left ischial groove

concepts.why: The presence of a solitary, completely cystic mass in the left L5–S1 foraminal zone, causing severe foraminal stenosis, along with neuropathic irritation of the left L4, L5, S1, and S2 roots, is consistent with a neurofibroma, particularly given the imaging characteristics and location along the course of the sciatic nerve.

The description of a cystic mass arising from the sciatic nerve, with peripheral rim enhancement and severe foraminal stenosis, is also consistent with a schwannoma, a type of nerve sheath tumor that can cause neuropathic symptoms and imaging findings similar to those described.

Although less common, perineurioma could also be considered given the location and imaging characteristics of the mass, as well as the presence of neuropathic irritation, though it is a less typical presentation compared to neurofibroma or schwannoma.
The severe neuropathic irritation at L5 and the large cystic mass along the sciatic nerve are consistent with a neurilemmoma.
